Users of the latest version of Claude Code on macOS and Linux can now have their various sessions send messages to each other to share findings, ask questions, and coordinate work. Here are the details.

Claude Code adds cross-session messaging feature

Anthropic announced a new feature earlier today that should be quite welcome for users who frequently run multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code v2.1.224, different sessions can send messages to each other, sharing updates and other relevant information; this feature is especially useful when users have multiple sessions handling different parts of the same project simultaneously.

Below is Anthropic's documentation for this new feature:

Anthropic says the best use cases for this new feature include: handing off research findings, coordinating parallel worktrees, checking the status of long-running tasks, and replying to messages across machines.

The company added that users do not need to write the message content themselves. Users simply enter what they want to convey in the prompt, and Claude will automatically compose the actual message.

It should be noted that the cross-session messaging feature does not apply to approving permission requests or changing settings. Commands such as /compact will appear as plain text rather than being executed as actual commands; if the receiving session requires permissions when processing a message, it will still prompt the user for approval.

For more information about the new Claude Code cross-session messaging feature, please visit this link.
